title: Vanishing from finite submodules by filtered colimits
statement: Let $h:Y\to X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $q\in\mathbf Z$, and $M$ a module over the universe lift of $\mathbf Z$. Let $n\in\mathbf N\setminus\{0\}$ annihilate every element of $M$. Write $\underline N$ for the constant module sheaf on the small etale site of $Y$ attached to a submodule $N\subseteq M$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. If $R^q h_*\underline N=0$ for every finite submodule $N$, then $R^q h_*\underline M=0$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The submodule index may live in the universe of $M$.

proof.text: Use Mathlib Module.fgSystem to index the inclusion diagram by finitely generated submodules of M in Type(u+1). Zero gives nonemptiness and sums give directedness. ModuleCat.directLimitIsColimit and Module.fgSystem.equiv construct its colimit and its linear equivalence with M. No arbitrary witness is chosen from an unproved existence theorem.

Each finitely generated lifted-integer submodule N is finitely generated over Z by scalar restriction. The nonzero integer n kills every element, witnessing torsion. Mathlib Module.finite_of_fg_torsion gives Finite N. The inherited lifted-integer module action equals the canonical one: write r as the cast of r.down and apply Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul. Thus hfinite applies to the diagram objects with its original signature.

Constant sheafification is a left adjoint and preserves the submodule colimit. Apply coefficient-size higher-direct-image preservation to this filtered index and compose the preserving functors. This handles every integer degree.

Every term of the resulting diagram is zero by hfinite. IsColimit.isZero_pt makes its colimit vertex zero. Transport along the image of Module.fgSystem.equiv under the composite functor, obtaining exactly the required vanishing for M. Zero M and n=1 are included.
